title: What is known about 1RB0LE_0LC0RB_1RD1LD_1RA1LF_0LB1LE_---1LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_0LC0RB_1RD1LD_1RA1LF_0LB1LE_---1LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. Its tape is a block of 1s at the left end and a word of short blocks on its right. The block is a clock: each tick makes it 3 cells longer and sends the head into the word twice as many times as the tick before; every trip rewrites the word by one fixed map P. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The clock is proved in Lean for every k: tick k applies P 2k times whenever the 2k trips all return (a hypothesis met by the actual run, checked in Lean for its first 15 trips). An exact accelerated simulator built on it follows the run through 65 phases to 6.04·10187 steps without a halt; what happens at a phase end (a trip that does not return) is not described by a formula.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when F reads a 0 (proved for every configuration). F is entered only from D reading a 1 (1LF, from the table), so a halt is the head in D on a 1 whose left neighbour is 0.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 144 cells have been visited and 100 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: B erases a block of 1s rightwards; E walks left over a block of 1s and stops on the 0 before it.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: A closed tape language with windows of 7 cells (search by bbtools.ctl, not checked in Lean) allows a halt only with F reading a 0 that is followed by 110010, 110011 or 110111.

claims.title: The tick, for every k
claims.text: If 2k P-steps (each a trip L 0 0 0 1 1 A> W → L E> 1^4 0 W' valid for every left tape L) take the word W to W' with total cost E, then L 0 0 0 E> 1^(4+3k) 0 W reaches L E> 1^(7+3k) 0 W' in exactly E + 19·2k − 3 steps. The tick is the sweep (the block becomes 0s), one P-step, the ticks 0, …, k−1 (each eats three of the 0s) and the merge.

claims.title: The clock carries the real run
claims.text: From step 470, where the run from blank tape is E> 1^4 0 W, the 15 P-steps of the next four ticks are proved for the actual words, and the tick theorem then takes the run to step 2,964, E> 1^16 0 W', exactly the configuration of the plain run there: the hypothesis of the tick is not vacuous.

claims.title: Accelerated simulator agrees with the plain run
claims.text: clock.py (the tick done at once, P computed by running the machine and memoized) gives the same time, block and word as tools/c/tmrun.c at all 50 visits of the left end in the first 1010 steps.

claims.title: No halt in 6.04·10<sup>187</sup> steps
claims.text: The exact accelerated run goes through 65 phases (a phase: ticks with the block growing by 3; it ends when a trip into the word does not return, the block is partly dissolved and a new phase starts from a somewhat shorter block). Last block followed: 1<sup>1858</sup>.

claims.title: Growth
claims.text: Phase after phase the block at a phase end and the word grow (blocks 34, 82, 139, 208, … at the ends of the first phases); a phase end shortens the block only a little. Nothing suggests a halt, but there is no formula for the phase end.

claims.title: The phase end
claims.text: What a failed trip does to the block and the word, and so whether some phase end ever reaches the halting configuration, is not known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. A block of 1s at the left end is a clock: tick k makes it 3 cells longer and sends the head 2<sup>k</sup> times into the word on its right, each trip applying one fixed rewrite P to the word.

facts.text: Tick k applies P 2<sup>k</sup> times whenever the 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return (Lean).
The block grows by 3 cells per tick (Lean, under the same condition).
Steps followed exactly (65 phases), no halt.

sections.heading: A clock and a word
html: Every so often the head, in state E, reaches the left end of the tape. One step before, the tape reads E>1 1^(3+3k) 0 W: a block of 4+3k ones, a 0, and a word W of short blocks of 1s separated by single or double 0s. Between two such visits the machine performs one tick.

A tick is built from smaller ticks. First the head sweeps the block into 0s. Then it makes one trip into the word, which rewrites the word's front by a fixed map P and rebuilds a block of four 1s. Then the ticks for blocks 4, 7, …, 1+3k run in turn, each eating three of the 0s the sweep left, and a merge joins the result to three 1s left behind. Counting trips: tick k makes 1 + 1 + 2 + … + 2k−1 = 2k of them, so tick k applies P exactly 2k times whenever all those trips come back, and takes E + 19·2k − 3 steps, E being the time spent in the trips. This is a Lean theorem for every k and every word.

sections.heading: The first ticks of the run
html: At step 470 the tape is E>1 1^3 0 1 0 1 0^2 1^7 0 1 0 1^4 0 1^4 0 1^2. Tick 0 (one trip) takes 161 steps: at step 631 the block is 17. Tick 1 (two trips) ends at step 966 with 110, tick 2 at 1,665 with 113, tick 3 at 2,964 with 116. All 15 trips of these four ticks are proved in Lean for the actual words, and the tick theorem then reproduces the run from blank tape to step 2,964 exactly.
The time per tick roughly doubles, so the block grows like the logarithm of the time.

sections.heading: Phases
html: A phase lasts as long as every trip comes back. It ends when one trip runs off the left end of its region: the unfinished ticks are abandoned, the block is partly taken apart, and a new phase begins with a somewhat shorter block and a longer word. An exact accelerated simulator that does each tick at once (checked against the plain C simulator at every visit in the first 1010 steps) gives:
It followed the run through 65 phases to 6.04·10187 steps; no halt. The block at a phase end keeps growing (11858 at the last one followed).

sections.heading: Where a halt could come from
html: The only halting transition is F reading a 0, and F is entered only from D reading a 1, so the machine halts exactly when D stands on a 1 with a 0 to its left. A tick whose trips all return is proved to finish, so a halt could only happen at a phase end, inside the trip that fails or the rebuild after it. None of the phase ends followed did so.

sections.heading: Open
html: Missing: a description of P2k on the words that occur, and a rule for what a phase end builds. With both, one could decide whether some phase end ever reaches the halting configuration; today only the long exact run says it has not yet.

summary: A clock at the left end: the block 1^(4+3k) grows by 3 per tick and tick k applies one word map P 2^k times to the word on its right whenever the 2^k trips into the word all return (proved in Lean for every k); followed exactly through 65 phases to 6.04·10^187 steps without a halt.
family: clock and word map (block grows by 3 at the left end)
